answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when one operator is caught running duplicate agents. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents earn theirs back. Like an ivory tower that admits only those who pay the entry price, or a pearl forming slowly layer by layer, standing should grow in a grove over time, not appear overnight, so cheap mass identities stay worthless.
